Cheer you up when you succeed.



—— Recommended consuming order ——

Step 1: Goal setting
If the goal is too big, break it down.

Step 2: only focus for 25 minutes
* Only focus on one thing
* Avoid distraction; make efforts to keep the Tomato running (ex. if someone hits you up, tell him/her getting back to you shortly!)
* Better to watch the timer counting

Step 3: Rest for 5 minutes
* Not suitable for mental consuming tasks
* Light activities that are good for your mind and body
* Pause your work momentarily can help you view things from another perspective and avoid couldn't see the forests for the trees. 

Step 4: Repeat 4 times, then take a more extended rest for 15 to 30 minutes
Repeat the previous two steps for 4 times, and take a 15 to 30 minutes long rest



—— After taking it, you can gain the following benefits on top of straight As —— 
* Prevent distracting and stay focused more easily: counting down timer brings good stress
* Reduce interruptions: postpone other tasks; most things can wait for 25 minutes
* Avoid procrastinating: when the timer is running, it means the declaration of a focused time frame
* Endure longer: with adequate rest, you can run further 



—— Features of “Focus Tomato” ——

Based on the Pomodoro method with new spice-ups and improvements.

* Do not force stop; keep the flow
Classical Promodoro clock asks you to stop working asap when time is up; Focus Tomato only notifies you with sound and does not force you to stop. You can keep staying in the zone and running the timer.

* Fractional time is allowed
Classical Promodoro clock requires to maintain 25 minutes duration. Focus Tomato freely lets you count the fractional time as long as it starts running.

* Modifiable Timeline
It is usual to forget to stop the timer. Focus Tomato allows you to modify the Timeline and make adjustments afterward.

* Do Not Disturb mode is available
Distracted by too many notifications? Do Not Disturb mode can be enabled when Focus Tomato is running.

* Integrate smoothly with other work methods and/or apps
Because the app only applies the timing part of the Promodoro technique, in addition to the original Promodoro method, you can also use the Reminder, Trello, or physical notebooks along with it.

title: Pomodoro
description: *****There are six steps in the original technique*****  1. Decide on the task to be done.  2. Set the Pomodoro timer (traditionally to 25 minutes).  3. Work on the task.  4. If you have fewer than four checkmarks, take a short break (3–5 minutes) and then return to step 2; otherwise continue to step 6.  6. After four Pomodoros, take a longer break (15–30 minutes), reset your checkmark count to zero, then go to step 1.Application developed by Linh Okita and Nyan.

This Chrome extension helps you focus on any task you are working on, such as studying, cooking, writing, or coding. 🍅 What is Pomodoro Timer? A Pomodoro Timer is a tool inspired by the Pomodoro Technique, a popular time management method developed in the late 1980s. It works by breaking down your work into intervals, typically 25 minutes long, called pomodoros (named after the Italian word for "tomato," inspired by the tomato-shaped kitchen timer the technique's creator used). These intervals are interspersed with short breaks, usually 5 minutes long, to help you maintain focus and avoid burnout. Here's how the Pomodoro Technique works: - Choose a task: Decide on what you want to accomplish in a pomodoro session. - Set the timer: Start your Pomodoro Timer for 25 minutes. - Work on the task: Focus solely on the chosen task until the timer rings. - Take a break: When the timer finishes, take a short break (5 minutes). Stand up, stretch, walk around, or do something relaxing that doesn't involve screens. - Repeat: After your break, start another Pomodoro session for the same task or a new one. - Longer breaks: After completing four Pomodoro sessions, take a longer break (15-30 minutes). 🚀The Pomodoro Technique is beneficial for several reasons: - Improves focus: By having shorter work intervals with breaks, you can prevent your mind from wandering and maintain better concentration. - Reduces procrastination: Knowing you only have 25 minutes to work on a task can make it less intimidating and encourage you to start. - Boosts productivity: By taking regular breaks, you refresh your mind and avoid burnout, leading to more productive work sessions. - Provides a sense of accomplishment: Completing Pomodoro sessions can give you a sense of progress and motivate you to keep working. # Pomodoro ™ and Pomodoro Technique ® are registered trademarks of Francesco Cirillo. #4 Minimalist Design: Clean, clutter-free interface that makes it easy for you to concentrate on what truly matters.

#5 Productivity Tracker: Keep an eye on your productivity trends and make changes to your work or study habits as needed.

The Pomodoro Technique is a well-structured time management method designed to maximize productivity and focus. Here's a quick tutorial on how to use it:

SELECT A TASK: Choose a task or set of tasks you intend to work on, whether it be studying for an exam or a work-related project.

SET THE POMODORO TIMER: Using a traditional timer, flip clock, or a tomato-shaped timer (pomodoro), set a 25-minute session. This is your time to focus on the selected task without interruption.

WORK ON THE TASK: Dedicate the next 25 minutes entirely to your chosen task. If a distraction pops up, write it down for later and immediately get back to your task.

END WORK WHEN THE TIMER ENDS: As soon as your pomodoro timer rings, stop working. This marks the end of one "Pomodoro" session.

TAKE A SHORT BREAK: After completing a pomodoro, take a 5-minute break. This allows your mind to rest and prepares you for the next session.
Repeat the Process: After your break, reset the timer and begin another 25-minute focus session.

LONG BREAKS: After completing four pomodoros, take a longer break—usually 15 to 30 minutes. This helps to prevent burnout and maintains a high level of productivity.

TRACK YOUR PROGRESS: Keep track of the number of pomodoros you complete in a day. This provides a clear picture of your productivity flow.

REMEMBER, the goal of the Pomodoro Technique is not to finish tasks—it's to work on them with full attention and without distractions. By breaking your work into manageable intervals (pomodoros), you train your brain to focus for short periods and improve your attention span over time.

Download Pomodoro Flip Clock today, and let the humble tomato help you optimize your time, maximize your focus, and boost your productivity. This is more than just a clock; it's a lifestyle upgrade.

title: Solace: Stay Focused
description:
Solace is a focus app for people who are tired of tricking themselves.

Most productivity apps rely on willpower. You tap a button, you promise yourself this session will be different, and ten minutes later you're back in the feed. Solace takes willpower out of the equation. To start a focus session, you physically scan an NFC tag. To end one, you scan the same tag again. That's it. If your tag is across the room, in another bag, or locked in a drawer, your distractions stay blocked — because getting back in means getting up.

Focus sessions in Solace use Apple's Screen Time system to block whatever pulls you off course:
  • Specific apps
  • Entire app categories
  • Websites
  • Adult content (optional)
  • In-app purchases (optional)
  • App installs and deletions (optional)

Create as many focus modes as you want — one for deep work, one for studying, one for reading, one for the gym. Pick a mode, scan your tag, and everything in that mode gets blocked until you scan again. Solace even prevents itself from being deleted during an active session, so you can't uninstall your way out of a commitment.

Alarms are gated the same way. Solace's optional alarm feature (iOS 26 and later) rings until you scan your tag. There's no snooze button, no slide-to-dismiss, no escape hatch. If you set the alarm, you're getting up.

WHAT MAKES SOLACE DIFFERENT

  • NFC-locked sessions — the tag is the key, not a password you can talk yourself around
  • Runs entirely on-device — no accounts, no cloud, no analytics, no trackers
  • Focus stats for today, this week, this month, and all time
  • Multiple focus modes for different contexts
  • Emergency unblocks for real life situations — used sparingly, gone when they're gone
  • A clean, dark-first interface built for SwiftUI and iOS

PRIVACY FIRST

Solace collects nothing. No sign-in. No email. No anonymous telemetry. No crash reporting from third parties. Your focus history, blocked apps, and alarm settings live on your device and nowhere else. When you delete Solace, every trace goes with it.

REQUIREMENTS

  • iPhone with NFC support (iPhone 7 or later)
  • iOS 17 or later for focus sessions
  • iOS 26 or later for the NFC-gated alarm
  • Any NDEF-writable NFC tag. Solace-branded tags are available, but any tag works.

GETTING STARTED

Open Solace, grant Screen Time and NFC permissions during the short onboarding, pick your first focus mode, and scan your tag. You're in.
